title: TS SDK: progressive-parse union adapters and Zod <-> JSON Schema bridging for streaming structured output
creator: Maya Rodriguez
description:
Problem: TypeScript SDK users need robust helpers to parse structured output from streaming LLM responses where the discriminating tag for a union type can arrive late or be split across chunks. Existing static codegen and Zod validators assume a full JSON payload; with streaming this causes frequent parse failures or requires buffering entire responses, which negates latency benefits.

Goal: Provide a runtime adapter layer and codegen/runtime helpers that enable: progressive-parsing of streaming JSON-like outputs, delayed-discriminator resolution for discriminated unions, graceful partial-validation with recovery hints, and automatic Zod <-> JSON Schema bridging for interoperability with evals and server-side validators. The solution should be ergonomic for SDK users (minimal API surface), compatible with existing ts-sdk typegen, and support retry/fallback semantics when parsing fails mid-stream.

High-level approach: 1) Add a streaming parser utility (parseStream<T>) that incrementally builds a parse tree and exposes events (partialObject, discriminatorResolved, finalObject). 2) Introduce union-hint metadata in generated runtime schemas so the parser can promote candidate branches as soon as minimal discriminator evidence is present. 3) Bridge Zod validators and generated JSON Schemas so users and server-side eval harnesses can reuse the same contracts. 4) Provide retry semantics hooks: onParseError -> allow automatic re-request with updated prompts / stricter schema or fallback to permissive union variant.

This ticket focuses on the TypeScript client runtime and typegen changes; follow-up tickets will add examples for Python/Go clients and Console/evals integration.
acceptance_criteria: parseStream<T>(schema, options) API implemented and exported from '@redwood/ts-sdk/runtime'
Generated typegen includes union-hint metadata in a non-breaking way (optional field in runtime schema)
Zod <-> JSON Schema roundtrip for generated schemas implemented and covered by unit tests
Streaming examples added to SDK docs and one end-to-end example in the examples/ directory showing streaming chat returning a union type
Integration test demonstrating successful parse when discriminating tag arrives in a later chunk without buffering full response
Retry hook implemented: callers can register onParseError to trigger a configured retry flow
Benchmark: parsing overhead < 5ms per ~1KB chunk on our CI baseline; end-to-end latency improvement vs full-buffering verified
implementation_steps: Design streaming parser API and event model (internal design doc link below)
Add runtime parser implementation using incremental JSON tokenizer tolerant to trailing commas and partial tokens
Augment typegen code to emit 'unionHints' metadata alongside Zod schemas; update codegen tests
Implement Zod->JSONSchema and JSONSchema->Zod helpers for generated artifacts
Expose parseStream in the public TS SDK and add types + docstrings
Add retry hook and sample retry policy provider in runtime (exponential backoff + prompt-append middleware)
Write unit tests for parser event stream, discriminator resolution heuristics, and recovery fallback
Create an end-to-end example app (examples/streaming-union) and add to CI smoke tests
Docs: add cookbook entry with code snippets and migration notes for existing users
risks: Complexity of incremental parsing could introduce subtle correctness bugs for deeply nested objects
UnionHint heuristics may be inaccurate and lead to optimistic branch selection causing validation surprises
Performance regression if parser allocations are not optimized; must benchmark on realistic streams
Backwards compatibility risk when introducing optional runtime schema fields in typegen
test_plan: Unit: tokenizer edge cases (split tokens, escaped characters, unicode)
Unit: union resolution with discriminator arriving first, middle, and last chunk
Integration: e2e against a mock streaming backend that emits realistic latency/fragmentation patterns
Fuzz: random chunk boundaries and interleaved control characters to validate parser tolerance
Perf: microbench parsing throughput and allocation profiles on CI runner
deploy_plan: Feature flag parseStream behind runtimeExperimental=true initially. Release under client-ts-2025.02 with a migration guide. Flip feature flag after 2 weeks of canary runs on internal apps and 1 week of open beta usage.
notes: We intentionally keep unionHints optional to avoid breaking existing generated schemas. Default runtime behavior is conservative: only resolve to a branch when a unique discriminator is present. Provide permissive fallback variant 'RawObject' to surface unparsable payloads to the application for manual handling.
